extracted.intended_audience: media, supporters, donors, and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: A nonprofit organization's press release announcing and explaining a funding decision (or reversal), communicating key facts, leadership statement, background, resources, and media contact information to journalists and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent headline summarizing the news
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear, bold headline that states the key news (example: 'Komen Foundation Restores Funding for Breast Cancer Screenings at Planned Parenthood Health Centers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concise sentence that communicates the primary development or announcement so readers immediately know the subject and outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release timing and dateline
rubrics_metrics.description: Include timing metadata such as 'For Immediate Release:' and the publication date (example shows 'For Immediate Release: Oct. 14, 2014' and 'Published February 03, 2012').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label whether the release is immediate and give the date so media know the timeliness and can cite the release appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update note for later developments
rubrics_metrics.description: When circumstances change after publication, add a prominent update line (example: 'UPDATE: February 3, 2012: The Susan G. Komen for the Cure Foundation reversed its decision...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place updates near the top and explicitly state the new facts so readers and reporters can see corrections or reversals at a glance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph summarizing core message and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: A short opening that summarizes the central news and its implications for the audience (example paragraphs explaining reversal, funds raised, and that 'every dollar... will go directly for breast exams and diagnostic services').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-load the most newsworthy facts: what happened, who is affected, and the immediate significance or impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official statement or quote from leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a labeled statement or quote from an organizational leader (example: 'Statement by Cecile Richards, Planned Parenthood Federation of America, Regarding Today’s Komen Announcement').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide authoritative voice and interpretation of the news; label the speaker and the context to give reporters a quotable source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression of thanks and call to action / engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Thank supporters and encourage engagement (example: 'Thank you so much for your voice and for standing with us. Join the conversation on facebook.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge supporters, include calls to action or social media prompts to sustain momentum and steer public engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background/context section
rubrics_metrics.description: A discrete 'Background' block explaining the context, stakes, and who is affected (example explains Komen's decision, the number of Planned Parenthood programs at risk, and services provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply journalists with concise historical/contextual information that helps them understand and report the story without additional research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-interest examples or patient stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Include short personal stories or case examples (example section titled 'Close to the Heart: Stories of Planned Parenthood Breast Care Patients' and 'Here are just a few of these stories.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a few concrete anecdotes that illustrate the real-world impact of the announcement and make the issue relatable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and informational links
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide links to relevant educational resources (examples: 'Learn more about breast exams.' and 'Learn more about mammograms.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer background material, fact sheets, or education links so reporters and the public can get more information and accurate context.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of related news coverage / press hits
rubrics_metrics.description: A curated 'In the News' list linking to media coverage of the issue (the page lists many outlets and story titles under 'In the News:').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show existing coverage to demonstrate newsworthiness, provide sources for additional reporting, and help media see the conversation's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational boilerplate/mission statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard closing paragraph describing the organization and its mission (example: 'Planned Parenthood is the nation’s leading provider... With more than 700 health centers across the country...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a brief, consistent summary of the organization that journalists can use in their stories and that orients unfamiliar readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source and media contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a 'Source' identifier and a clear media contact with phone number (example: 'Source: Planned Parenthood Federation of America' and 'Contact Planned Parenthood Federation of America media office: 212-261-4433').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include a named contact and phone/email so reporters can reach someone for interviews, fact-checking, or follow-up.
